Suppress them? No... no, I wouldn't say I try to suppress or ignore them at all. I know I just said a moment ago that I wish I could turn it off because it’s so incredibly exhausting, but it’s not like I’m actively fighting to push the thoughts out of my mind. I feel this intense, almost moral obligation to sit there and dissect every single second of that appointment. I’ll sit on the edge of my bed for hours, just staring at the floor, replaying the exact words I used, wondering if my tone was dismissive, or if I missed a sign of something much worse. 

It’s not like some bizarre, random thought popping into my head out of nowhere that I have to bat away. It’s just this heavy, undeniable truth that I’m doing harm. So, no, I don't suppress them. If anything, I lean into them, because if I were to just ignore those thoughts, wouldn't that just make me an even more negligent doctor? A responsible physician is supposed to reflect on their shortcomings, right? So I just let the thoughts play out, over and over, analyzing every detail, even though it completely drains whatever energy I have left for the day. I just... I feel like I deserve to feel awful about it, because it's my fault, so ignoring it isn't really an option for me.

In line with how I want to be? Well... no, I mean, obviously not. I don't think anyone goes into medicine *wanting* to be a bad doctor. Part of myself? I mean... I don't know if I'd use those exact words, but I guess, in a way, yes. It’s hard to explain without sounding completely unhinged, but it’s like... they aren't just thoughts anymore. Values... I mean, when you talk about values, the very first thing that comes to mind is the oath, right? "First, do no harm." That is the foundational value of my entire adult life. Yes, they are completely consistent with what I believe about myself, because I firmly believe I have failed all of those values. I know I touched on this a minute ago, but it's just so consuming... it's why I can't stop obsessing over the records. Even when I review the chart and there’s absolutely no evidence of a bad outcome—like, the patient is discharged, they are at home, their labs are stone-cold normal—I still keep believing that some routine delay on my part, or some slightly imperfect message I sent to the floor nurses, has quietly harmed them. 

It’s like my brain completely bypasses the objective data. I’ll see a perfectly stable patient, but because I know I took an extra twenty minutes to respond to a page because I was tied up, or because my phrasing in a handoff wasn't flawlessly precise, I believe with every fiber of my being that I've set a tragedy in motion. I've violated my core value of doing no harm, even if the harm is invisible right now. And because I value honesty, the fact that I'm just sitting here, going to work every day while this quiet damage is out there... it feels like a massive betrayal. I'm just carrying around this heavy, sinking belief that it's all going to catch up to me, and that everyone will eventually discover exactly how much I've failed these people. 

So it’s this horrible paradox. The thoughts are completely opposed to the values I hold dear, but they perfectly match the belief I have that I am, at my core, a failure who has irreparably compromised those values. I don't know if that distinction makes sense to anyone but me, but it’s just how my mind is processing everything right now. I just can't shake the belief that I'm a walking violation of everything I ever stood for.

Intrusive... I mean, when you use that word, intrusive, it makes it sound like... like a fly buzzing into a room through an open window, you know? Like something that absolutely doesn't belong there, something foreign that just suddenly pops into your head and you want to swat it away because it's annoying and out of place. It's not like I'm sitting there having a perfectly normal day, feeling confident about my clinical judgment, and then out of nowhere this weird, random thought just barges in to ruin it. I wouldn't say they enter my mind without me wanting them to, because it's really not about wanting or not wanting. It's just... it's just the reality of my situation. It's like... if you look outside and it's pouring rain. You don't have an "intrusive" thought that it's raining. You just see the rain, and you know it's raining, whether you actually want it to be raining or not. You're just observing a fact. 

That's exactly how my brain is operating with all of this. I'm not having these unwanted, random thoughts about being a danger to my patients... I'm just constantly, painfully aware of the fact that I am. It's just there. It's the baseline. Like, even yesterday, I was driving home from the clinic, and I had the radio on, just some local jazz station trying to... I don't know, distract myself for five minutes. And it wasn't like a thought suddenly intruded over the music. It's more like the music was just this incredibly thin, useless layer over this deep, ocean-level certainty that I had missed something critical on a patient's chart earlier that afternoon. 

So it's not an invader. It's just me. It's just my own brain processing what I believe is the absolute, undeniable truth about my incompetence. So, no, I really wouldn't call them intrusive. I hear what you're trying to do. You're trying to introduce logic, right? You're asking if there's a sliver of a chance, a one percent possibility that I'm wrong and they're perfectly fine. And logically, if I were looking at someone else's case, maybe I'd say yes. It's not a 'what if' or a passing anxiety. It's a certainty that the harm is already done, it's just incubating. It's hiding in the margins. 

And the part that makes it unbearable, the part that makes my chest just ache all day and keeps me pacing the floor at night, is that I know everyone will eventually discover it. It's only a matter of time before the hospital administration, or the morbidity and mortality committee, or the family pulls the records, connects the dots, and sees exactly what my incompetence caused. They're going to see that I was the weak link. So... no. When you ask if it's possible they aren't being harmed... it just doesn't feel possible to me at all. It feels like a guaranteed disaster that just hasn't officially dropped yet, and it doesn't matter one bit what the objective data in the chart says today, because tomorrow is when they'll finally see what I've done.
